column3: NASB adds “certain” (Hebrew “one man”) and renders “an Ephrathite” as “an Ephraimite.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“From days to days” becomes “yearly,” and לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֹת (“to bow down”) is rendered “to worship.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB uses habitual “would give” for the repeated yearly practice.
“A double portion” renders an obscure phrase (literally “one portion of two faces”); the meaning is uncertain.
NASB renders “also provocation” as “bitterly” and “to disconcert her” as “to irritate her.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a year in a year” becomes “year after year.”

“Hard of spirit” is rendered “oppressed in spirit.”
“Do not give your maidservant before a daughter of worthlessness” becomes “Do not consider your maidservant as a worthless woman”; “greatness of complaint” becomes “great concern.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says her face “was no longer to her”; NASB supplies “sad.”
“Knew Hannah” is rendered “had relations with Hannah,” and “bowed down” as “worshiped.”
“At the circuit of the days” becomes “in due time,” and NASB supplies “saying” before Hannah’s words.
“The sacrifice of the days” is rendered “the yearly sacrifice.”
NASB supplies “I will not go up”; “until perpetuity” is rendered “forever.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew reads “with three bulls”; NASB’s “a three-year-old bull” follows a different reading. “Skin of wine” becomes “jug,” and “the lad was a lad” becomes “the child was young.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The opening plea (“please, my lord”) is rendered “Oh, my lord!”; “by the life of your soul” becomes “As your soul lives.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The verb “ask/lend” (also in “asked”) is rendered “dedicated” twice, so the play on asking is less visible; “bowed down” becomes “worshiped.”
